The output voltage and current relations for the ZVS dual SEPIC with multiple outputs are derived, and a design procedure is given. A simple conceptual model is developed of the coupled inductors and power transformers on a common core, and the effect of using quasiresonant switching on the zero-ripple condition is examined. A 36 V to 5 and 15 V experimental prototype is constructed, and total ripple and noise voltages of less than 3 mV peak are observed on both outputs.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Simulated ONUs for battery characterization in the local loop: a status report
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] Fourteenth International Telecommunications Energy Conference - INTELEC '92
abstract: In fiber-in-the-loop systems power to the optical network units (ONUs) that are located at the far end of the fiber can be provided by local powering, in which power is supplied by a commercial power source located near the ONU; when this source fails, power is supplied by batteries co-located with the ONU. To determine if small battery systems can be made to exhibit 7 to 10 year lives in a New York/New Jersey climate, a field demonstration was conducted. The batteries used were longer-lived and more reliable than typical consumer batteries and redundancy was used in the battery system. Eleven ONUs, with simulated power loads and simulated power outages, have been operating with representative battery systems for the 30 months. The basic battery system design is described, and a status report on the field demonstration is given.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A new generic family of saturable reactor-assisted soft-switching PWM DC-DC converters for high-power density distributed power systems
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] Fourteenth International Telecommunications Energy Conference - INTELEC '92
abstract: A generic family of high power density DC-DC power converter topologies with high-frequency AC link and without transformer isolation link is described. A saturable reactor assisted (SRA) soft switching mode constant frequency pulse width modulation (PWM) technique efficiently operates at a zero voltage switching transition scheme. This kind of quasi-trapezoidal wave mode PWM DC-DC power converter incorporates a small saturable reactor or a few saturable reactors in order to achieve efficient soft switching commutated operation. The use of the converter family results in much higher switching operation with a high efficiency and a quick control response. A simple forward/flyback hybrid type SRA asymmetrical PWM soft switching DC-DC power converter with high frequency link, which is included in one of the SRA soft switched PWM converter topologies, is demonstrated and theoretically analyzed in steady-state operation. Key experimental results are shown and discussed using a 150 W, 200 kHz MOSFET power converter breadboard implementation.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Maintenance management by utilizing dynamic intelligence-implementations and experiences
publicationTitle: [Proceedings] Fourteenth International Telecommunications Energy Conference - INTELEC '92
abstract: Optimal uncertainty management schemes are defined and an implementation is described. These facilities have been in trial use for a year in three power supply systems. The optimal schemes stipulate that the onsite supervision facilities take care of brute uncertainty management work. The dynamic intelligence of power system expert(s) is used to verify the most probable explanations sent by the onsite facilities. The process is most effective if the upper level or service terminal software supports the human way of reasoning.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
